CVE-2026-112072.description: vault-java-driver, a Java client for HashiCorp Vault, parses Vault's JSON responses with a vendored minimal-json parser that has no nesting depth limit. CVE-2026-99502.title: s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup
CVE-2026-99502.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

s390/pci: Fix double-free and NULL deref in zpci MSI domain cleanup

zpci_remove_parent_msi_domain() dereferences zbus->msi_parent_domain
unconditionally and does not clear it afterwards.

zpci_bus_create_pci_bus() removes the domain when pci_create_root_bus()
fails, then zpci_bus_release() removes it again on the last kref_put(),
reading ->fwnode from the freed irq_domain and freeing it twice.

If zpci_alloc_domain() or zpci_create_parent_msi_domain() fails, no domain
is created at all; zbus is kzalloc'd, so the same release path dereferences
NULL.

Return early when there is no domain, and clear the pointer after removing
one.

CVE-2026-99788.title: ACPI: CPPC: Validate FFH register fields before hardware access
CVE-2026-99788.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ACPI: CPPC: Validate FFH register fields before hardware access

The x86 CPPC FFH accessors construct masks and shift values using the
firmware's Bit Width and Bit Offset without checking that the field fits
in an MSR. A zero-width field or a field extending beyond bit 63 can
therefore cause an invalid shift. The safe MSR accessors only handle an
access fault, not invalid field arithmetic after a successful read.

Also, the 64-bit GAS address is implicitly narrowed to the 32-bit MSR
number. A descriptor with nonzero upper address bits can access a different
MSR from the one described by firmware.

The arm64 AMU counter readers have the same unchecked field arithmetic.

descriptors in the paired counter path.
